search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; measurement-validity/benchmark-design; finite-horizon anytime-valid paired evaluation under nuisance discordance rate

public_primary_sources.title: Optimal Anytime-Valid Tests for Composite Nulls
public_primary_sources.used_scope: For iid finite-alphabet composite nulls, a universal e-process formed from a universal predictor divided by the running null MLE is first-order optimal as alpha->0. Used as an asymptotic/composite benchmark, not as a finite-horizon optimality claim.

public_primary_sources.title: Time-sensitive anytime-valid testing
public_primary_sources.authors: Eugenio Clerico; Tobias Wegel; Iskander Azangulov; Patrick Rebeschini
public_primary_sources.used_scope: Reward-sensitive testing-by-betting; Markov reduction and Bellman control over time and wealth; hard deadlines can require objectives different from GRO. Full equivalence to arbitrary e-processes is only claimed in the simple-null/simple-alternative case, so our composite-null use is restricted to the explicitly valid sign-betting action class.

public_primary_sources.title: Learning to Bet for Horizon-Aware Anytime-Valid Testing
public_primary_sources.authors: Ege Onur Taga; Samet Oymak; Shubhanshu Shekhar
public_primary_sources.used_scope: Finite-horizon control for bounded means; aggressive bets can be preferable when behind schedule and horizon-aware policies can beat Kelly-style asymptotic bets. Used as qualitative support for horizon-dependent betting, not direct evidence for matched-pair tests.

public_primary_sources.title: Gaussian-efficient testing by betting on the mean of bounded data
public_primary_sources.used_scope: Very recent bounded-mean method designs predictable betting fractions to track conditional rejection probability of a powerful terminal Gaussian test and reports finite-sample-valid martingale-dependence intervals with iid Gaussian efficiency. Used as a design lead for terminal-test-informed forward bets, not as a matched-pair result.

public_primary_sources.title: E-values for k-Sample Tests With Exponential Families
public_primary_sources.authors: Yunda Hao; Peter Grünwald; Tyron Lardy; Long Long; Reuben Adams
public_primary_sources.used_scope: Shows conditional e-variables can remove nuisance structure by conditioning on sufficient statistics in exponential-family k-sample tests. Used as conceptual support for nuisance-elimination by conditioning, not as proof of the matched-pair identity below.

new_derivation.matched_pair_model: Each task produces + (candidate-only success), - (incumbent-only success), or 0 (concordant). Under the iid common-rho McNemar null, P_rho(+)=rho/2, P_rho(-)=rho/2, P_rho(0)=1-rho. Let d=w+l and c=n-d.
new_derivation.KL_inf: For alternative P(+)=rho1*q, P(-)=rho1*(1-q), P(0)=1-rho1, minimizing KL(P||P_rho) over rho sets rho=rho1 and gives gamma*=rho1*[q log(2q)+(1-q)log(2(1-q))]. Thus discordance rate multiplies sign-information; concordance contributes no KL once rho is fitted.
new_derivation.conditional_sign_e_factor: For any predictable a_t in [0,1], use factor 2a_t on +, 2(1-a_t) on -, and 1 on 0. Under any past-dependent null with conditional P(+|past)=P(-|past)=rho_t/2, its conditional expectation is exactly 1. This removes rho_t without estimating it and remains valid beyond iid common-rho.
new_derivation.KT_factorization: For a Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2) universal mixture, reparameterizing p+=rho*q, p-=rho*(1-q), p0=1-rho factorizes the prior into q~Beta(1/2,1/2) and rho~Beta(1,1/2). Therefore E_full_KT(n)=E_sign_Jeffreys(d,w)*R_rho(n,d), where R_rho = [Beta(d+1,c+1/2)/Beta(1,1/2)] / [(d/n)^d (c/n)^c], with 0^0 terms interpreted by continuity.
new_derivation.pathwise_dominance: Because the rho-mixture likelihood is an average of rho-likelihoods while the denominator is their supremum, 0<R_rho<=1 for every sequence/state. Hence the nuisance-conditioned sign Jeffreys e-process is pointwise at least as large as this full KT universal composite e-process at every time. At n=50,d=20,c=30, R_rho≈0.11139 (log penalty -2.1947), a roughly 9x evidence penalty before thresholding.
new_derivation.scope: The pointwise factorization/dominance is algebraic for the stated factorized KT mixture and null-MLE statistic. Shekhar's first-order optimality applies under iid finite-alphabet assumptions; the broader predictable-rho validity statement applies to the conditional sign factors, not automatically to the full universal-MLE process.

finite_horizon_computation.baseline_method: Exact state-probability dynamic programming over (w,l,c) with absorbing threshold log E >= log 20 for full KT, sign-Jeffreys mixture, and oracle fixed a=q GRO bet.
finite_horizon_computation.horizon_method: Numerical Bellman recursion over (remaining rounds, log wealth) within the valid conditional-sign action class a in [0.5,0.9995]. Grid interpolation used; no claim of global optimality over arbitrary composite-null e-processes.
finite_horizon_computation.interpretation: At short deadlines the Bellman policy deliberately bets much more aggressively than the GRO/Kelly alternative q=0.75; as T grows, its initial bet moves back toward q. This directly demonstrates that asymptotic growth optimality and finite-horizon resolution are different evaluation objectives.
finite_horizon_computation.validity_note: Every Bellman-selected one-step factor is a conditional e-variable under sign-symmetry, so any predictable policy retains Ville type-I control. The reported Bellman power values are numerical approximations; the three baseline crossing probabilities are exact for the specified iid alternative and state-based statistics.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: When an exact conditional symmetry removes a nuisance parameter, condition/skip it before applying a generic universal composite-null e-process; otherwise universal coding/MLE regret for the nuisance can materially delay finite-horizon decisions.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: In the matched-pair trinomial model, the KT universal statistic factors exactly into the Jeffreys sign e-process times a nuisance mixture-to-MLE factor <=1. The factor is ~0.111 at n=50,d=20, so the conditional sign process is pathwise larger for the same sign mixture. Shekhar still guarantees first-order optimality of the generic finite-alphabet universal route under iid assumptions, showing that first-order optimality does not imply finite-horizon dominance.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Exact for the stated McNemar sign-symmetry null and factorized Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2) universal mixture. Do not generalize to arbitrary nuisance parameters or arbitrary universal predictors without deriving the factorization/conditional null.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.implication: Evaluation pipelines should search for exact conditionings/ancillaries that eliminate nuisance before paying universal-prediction regret, especially when only 10-50 independent tasks are available.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Optimize the actual decision-time utility (e.g. rejection by deadline) over valid predictable bets, rather than assuming a GRO/Kelly or universal-asymptotic strategy is best at finite horizon.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: For alpha=.05, rho=.4, q=.75, the numerical Bellman policy within the sign-betting class achieved approximate reject-by-T probabilities 0.097/0.327/0.478/0.700 at T=10/20/30/50. Oracle fixed GRO achieved 0.00123/0.0758/0.2438/0.5388; sign Jeffreys 0.00731/0.1044/0.1799/0.3331; full KT 0.000126/0.0192/0.0579/0.1284. The Bellman initial bet shifted ~0.9995 -> 0.9166 -> 0.8117 -> 0.7428 as horizon increased.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Power comparison is for one iid alternative and a numerically discretized Bellman solution restricted to the conditional-sign e-factor action class. It is not a proof that this policy is globally optimal among all e-processes for the composite null.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.implication: Meta-evaluation of sequential evaluators should declare the reward/deadline and report horizon-specific resolved probability, not only asymptotic log-growth or eventual power.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Use terminal-test rejection geometry to design predictable forward bets, avoiding arbitrary composite backward decompositions while retaining finite-sample martingale validity.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Martinez-Taboada & Ramdas (2026-08-22) explicitly design betting fractions that track conditional rejection probability of a powerful terminal Gaussian test, with nonasymptotic validity under conditional-mean martingale dependence and iid Gaussian efficiency. This supplies a fresh design template directly adjacent to the previous backward-induction frontier.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Published result is for bounded-mean confidence intervals, not McNemar/matched pairs. Applying it to discordant signs requires a new derivation and cannot be assumed.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.implication: Derive a terminal-exact-binomial/McNemar rejection-tracking predictable bet on discordant signs and compare it with Bellman deadline-optimal and Jeffreys/no-regret bets.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: A first-order optimal universal composite e-process is automatically the best evaluator for 10-50-task deadlines.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. First-order optimality is alpha->0/asymptotic expected-stopping optimality. The matched-pair KT instantiation pays a finite nuisance-regret factor and was much weaker than conditioned sign processes in the specified finite-horizon calculation.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Oracle GRO/Kelly betting at the true alternative maximizes probability of resolving before a hard deadline.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected in the tested setting. A time/wealth-dependent Bellman policy had much higher reject-by-deadline probability and intentionally used more aggressive early bets at short horizons.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: The numerical Bellman result proves global optimality for the composite McNemar null.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. The DP optimizes only over a specified conditional-sign e-variable action class. Clerico et al.'s no-loss equivalence with arbitrary e-processes is established for simple-null/simple-alternative settings, not this composite null.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: The fresh Gaussian-efficient betting paper directly solves matched-pair sequentialization.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. It gives a design principle for bounded means; a matched-pair conditional-sign derivation remains open.

design_implications.gate_1: Before generic composite-null sequentialization, test whether nuisance can be exactly conditioned out while preserving the intended estimand and filtration.
design_implications.gate_2: Separate asymptotic growth optimality from finite-horizon decision utility. Choose and report the actual reward/deadline objective.
design_implications.gate_3: For horizon-aware policies, report the action class and whether claimed optimality is within-class or over all valid e-processes.
design_implications.gate_4: For finite-horizon numerical policies, publish grid/convergence or other approximation diagnostics and exact baseline calculations.
